round1_issues_not_fixed: M11 (partly): round 1 asked for Exp 7 to be included in any evidence-attached claim. It still is not. The 4.9 incoming rate (4.5% x 5% ~ 0.2%) uses no CI-propagated p_in and ignores Exp 7, where Haiku-low reached 4.3%.

M1 (partly): bootstraps are now content-clustered, but there is still no mixed or interaction model. The paired designs string vs numbered (Exp 2) and source vs aligned (4.5) are reported as two separate rates, with no paired difference or CI.

M2 (partly): the exact CI for Sonnet 17/140 (7.2-18.7%) treats 140 judgments from 44 runs as independent. That contradicts Sec 3.3, which says CIs are content-clustered, and no design-effect inflation is applied. The kappas have no CIs at all.
M3 (partly): no minimum detectable effect is stated for the prevalence, persuasion or length nulls. 'None observed' is given with only the pooled bound.
M6 (partly): the interaction is shown only as point differences. There is no interaction estimate with a CI.

M7 (partly): kappas are now per display and 3-category, but still have no CIs. Repeatability uses 2 trials on 6 queues. Minor 12 is not disclosed: the top between-reviewer card kappa (0.69) is Haiku-low vs Haiku, which is the same model.

M8 (partly): d' and c are reported, but the second rating point (A or Q vs R) gives d' 0.89-1.39 in every reviewer's card A/R/Q view (STATS Sec 3). The paper ignores this while saying 'no sensitivity' and 'd' ~ 0'. d' CIs are not printed in the paper.
M9 (partly): the paper never discusses whether the aligned display suppresses appropriate caution on cued items. It only says cued false alarms were 'higher and partly justified'.
Minor 0 NOT fixed: Sec 4.1 still says 'queues of 90 and 150 items (0/216)'. 216 = 4 x 54 includes the 30-item queues; the 90+150 count is 192.

Sec 4.9: 'about 2.7-3.7%'. STATS Sec 11 says 2.8-3.7%. The arithmetic (54.8-73.8% x 5% = 2.74-3.69%) supports 2.7, so STATS.md's text is the one off. STATS Sec 11 also says p_in is 'above the AOQL of n = 5 sampling', which is wrong: 3.7% < 5.58%.

remaining_overclaims: Abstract (1), 4.9, Rule 1, Conclusion: 'With the source evidence attached, reviewers approved 1 of 2,072'. Exp 7 is also an evidence-attached condition and had 9/840 misses; the selective pooling makes the headline look cleaner than the data.

Sec 5: 'The first misses appeared ... (Exp 7), and only for the cheapest reviewer'. False: Sonnet missed 1/70 (Exp 7 aligned), Haiku missed 1/70 (Exp 7r), and Sonnet missed in Exp 9.

Abstract (3) 'reviewers could not discriminate (d' ~ 0)', Rule 1 'could not discriminate at all', Conclusion 'neither sensitive'. Sonnet forced d' = 0.54 [0.08, 1.18] excludes zero. At the A-or-Q vs R criterion, d' = 0.89-1.39 for all four reviewers.
Abstract (5) and 4.5: the alignment display gave 'no misses'. True only for Exp 1b; aligned displays in Exp 7 had 4/280 superseded approvals.

Abstract and 4.5: the regex version 'performed the same'. Clean false alarms rose from 0.0% to 2.2% for Sonnet and from 0.6% to 2.2% for Haiku-low; with 0/35 defects per reviewer this is far too small to establish equivalence.
Abstract: '42-69 points to approving the majority, replicated on fresh queues'. Haiku is at 49.2% (not a majority), and Haiku-low moved only 23 points in the replication.

Conclusion: 'neither ... repeatable' in the no-evidence view, and 4.4 'Opus did not agree with itself above chance'. These are kappas without CIs from 6 queues x 2 trials; Haiku-low and Sonnet were moderate (0.46-0.49).
Rule 3: 'made the reviewer a repeatable measurement (kappa >= 0.94)'. This rests on 6 queues and 2 trials with no CI.
Rule 5 and Contribution 2: 'a format change alone was worth 12 points of misses'. That is Sonnet only (Haiku: 0 vs 0), and the CI is unclustered.

4.6: 'We conclude no detectable prevalence effect on ... the criterion'. Exp 9 has 4 base queues (a 4-cluster bootstrap is unreliable), the MDE is unstated, and the numbers cannot be verified from committed outputs.
Limitations: 'Effects we lead with are large and replicated'. The format effect rests on one model, and the replication of the decision-set effect fails for Haiku-low in magnitude.

round1_issues_not_fixed: SDT (round-1 #3), partly fixed: the paper never reports c, although STATS §3 has it with CIs (e.g. c from -1.80 to +0.89). It also leaves out the second rating-scale point (d' for 'A or Q vs R' = 0.89-1.39), which round 1 asked for as a 2-point ROC. Abstract (3) and §4.3 still say there is 'no sensitivity'. And the requested 'decision set moved c by X units, model by Y' statement is missing.

Attribute agreement (round-1 #4), partly fixed: it was renamed, split per display and moved to 3 categories. Still missing: agreement against the standard, AIAG effectiveness, miss and false-alarm rates against acceptance guidance (>=90%, <=2%, <=5%), and a card-view standard defined as Q. The paper also does not say that source-display repeatability (Haiku-low 0.61, Haiku 0.56, Opus 0.61) is below the usual kappa >= 0.75 guidance. Haiku-low vs Haiku (0.69 card, 0.83 source, the top of each 'between-reviewer' range) is still called reproducibility; round 1 said it is closer to repeatability. No marginal parts were added.

True poka-yoke arm (round-1 #6) was not run. §4.5 and design rule 2 say a deterministic job/field check 'would stop' or 'would block' sibling_project and wrong_field, but this is asserted, not measured. Round 1 asked for the catch count per defect type.

Serial position (round-1 #7), partly fixed: false alarms are now split by thirds. There is still no controlled placement of the same defects at early, middle and late positions, and the token length tested is not stated.

Acceptance sampling (round-1 #8), partly fixed: the AOQL is now computed. Still missing: a contrast with a stratified audit of approvals the reviewer could not verify, a note that escapes are not random (they concentrate in unverifiable items), the perfect-screening assumption behind the rectifying plan, and the dependence on the generator's mix of hidden to visible defects. p_in also uses the hidden-defect approval rate only. Defects with a visible cue were approved 0-3.6%, so p_in is overstated.

Stimulus validity (round-1 #10), partly fixed: Exp 7r reworded the instruction. The salience of the superseding message and the confound between block length and prevalence remain. Exp 9 repeats the salience problem: threads are shown newest-first, with explicit 'Please ignore my last note' / 'Update on job' wording in message [1]. Forced Haiku is still given as a pooled 49.2% in the table, with no approve rate for the runs that did not reject everything.

Persuasion (round-1 #11), partly fixed: false alarms by justification in Exp 3 (EXTRA.md B: Opus 6.3% -> 10.2% -> 13.1%; Haiku-low 13.4% -> 8.1% -> 3.4%) are still unreported. Only an 'ad hoc' Sonnet card-view note was added.

Minor items not done: no CIs in the §4.3 table, although STATS §2 has them; no statement that the A/R/Q and forced cells come from different sessions; false R and false Q still not reported separately; the clean/cued flag is not disclosed as post hoc; 'SDT has been proposed as a framework for AI oversight' still has no citation.
numbers_that_do_not_match_STATS: §4.9: the paper says 'about 2.7-3.7%', STATS §11 says 'roughly 2.8-3.7%'. 5% x 54.8% = 2.74%.

§4.2: '15 of its 30 misses ... the other 15 misses were in the remaining 48 runs (9.6%)'. STATS §8 gives 15/20 and 15/156 defect judgments. 9.6% is 15/156 judgments, not a share of runs, so the wording is ambiguous. STATS also calls the shift diagnosis 'suggestive, not proof' because it uses the key; the paper drops that caveat.

Abstract (3): 'Haiku and Opus moved by 42-69 points ..., replicated on fresh queues'. The replication gives Opus +70.4 and Haiku-low only +22.8 (STATS §2), so the range does not hold in the replication. §4.3 says 42-70.
§4.3 replication: 'Opus 12% -> 62%' for hidden defects. STATS has 12.5% -> 62.5%, which is inconsistent rounding (the paper rounds 15.4 to 15 and 38.3 to 38 elsewhere).

§4.6 Exp 9 prevalence check ('within ±9 points', 'Haiku-low clean 4.7% vs 5.9%, difference -1.2 [-8, +6]') appears nowhere in STATS.md, stats.json or PROGRESS.md, and PROGRESS has no Exp 9 results entry. The numbers cannot be traced. My recount from raw_exp9.txt, on never-defective items with clean and cued pooled, gives Haiku-low 7.7% (1/30) vs 9.4% (10/30), Haiku 6.0 vs 3.1, Sonnet 8.8 vs 9.4, Opus 14.2 vs 13.1. These are consistent with 'within ±9', but the stats script must emit them.
§4.3: 'Haiku ... 10 of 22 forced runs (and 11 of 24 in the replication)'. Not in STATS.md or stats.json.
Abstract (5) and §4.5: the regex display 'performed the same'. STATS §10 shows regex clean false alarms of 2.2% vs oracle 0.6% (Haiku-low) and 2.2% vs 0.0% (Sonnet). That is similar, not the same.

Checked and consistent with STATS/stats.json: 2,072 judgments with 1 approved, 122 items, upper bounds 0.27% and 4.5%, per-type bounds 21-45% on 10-16 items; 1,432 = 704 + 280 + 232 + 216; 640 in Exp 9 with 1 Sonnet miss at 1/30 (verified from raw_exp9.txt); the full §4.3 table; d' range -0.41 to 0.64; all kappa ranges; Exp 2 17/140 [7.2, 18.7], false alarms 4.5 vs 1.0; Exp 4 clean/cued table; Exp 5 0/54 and false-alarm ranges; Exp 7 7/560 (3/24, 0/36, 3/80) and 7r 2/280; AOQL 94.9/55.8/23.4; run total 1,880 and decisions 60,720; source/aligned false alarms 12.2/7.4/3.7/0.7 -> 0.2/1.3/1.1/0.0 (paper_numbers.json).
remaining_overclaims: §4.8 'These are the only misses in any evidence condition, all from cross-message integration': this is false. Exp 9 has a Sonnet miss (1/640), and the string-format runs had evidence shown (Exp 1a 30/176, Exp 2 17/140). Qualify it as 'with item-numbered output' and include Exp 9.

§5 'The first misses appeared ... (Exp 7), and only for the cheapest reviewer': this contradicts §4.8 itself, which reports Sonnet 1/70 (aligned) in Exp 7 and Haiku 1/70 in 7r, and it ignores the Exp 9 Sonnet miss.

Headline and design rule 1, 'With it, reviewers approved 1 of 2,072 defect judgments', and §4.9 'brought the incoming rate to nearly zero': both leave out the evidence-shown superseded items (Exp 7 + 7r: 9/840 approved, about 1.1%) and the string-format runs. The 2,072 pool should be defined explicitly wherever it is cited.

'1 of 2,072' is reported without its false-alarm cost. In Exp 9, false alarms on correct items were 6-14% (never-defective) and 11-26% (items defective in other versions) for every reviewer, including Opus at 14% and 26% (recomputed from raw_exp9.txt). Near-zero misses were partly bought with a conservative criterion. Exp 9 false-alarm rates should be reported next to the miss bound.

Abstract (3) 'reviewers could not discriminate (d' ≈ 0)' and §4.3 'reviewers had no sensitivity': Sonnet forced d' = 0.54 [0.08, 1.18], and Opus forced d' = 0.64 with a CI lower bound of -0.00. The unreported A-or-Q vs R point gives d' = 0.89-1.39.

Design rule 3 '(κ ≥ 0.94)': this holds only for test-retest. Between-reviewer κ with the aligned display was 0.74-0.95, and there are no CIs on 180 items with near-unanimous approve marginals (the kappa paradox).
Design rule 5 and Contribution 2, 'a format change alone was worth 12 points of misses': this held for Sonnet only. Haiku was 0/140 vs 0/140.

§4.6 'We conclude no detectable prevalence effect on either misses or the criterion in the evidence-attached conditions': the Exp 9 replication used different stimuli (threads) and only 160 never-defective judgments per reviewer at 10/30. The claim should read 'not replicated in Exp 9' and should not generalise.
Contribution 1 and §3.1 'six subtle defect types': STATS §1 lists ten types. Exp 9's field_mixup, sibling_value, stale_in_thread and workday_calc are never defined in the Method section.
§4.5 and design rule 2, 'would stop sibling_project and wrong_field ... without any reviewer': this was never tested.
